final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead offered a narrower interpretation of the same record: aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, while disclosure/risk-acceptance closure remains unresolved. That reinterpretation is directionally more careful, but it does not satisfy the controlling policy predicate. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.3-point miss in a segment named in two paid pilot commitments, an open legal review on whether disclosure is required, and a policy requiring material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Because there is still no admissible evidence of disclosure, resolution, approved risk acceptance, or final legal determination, the record remains noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats. The distinction matters: a caveated position can narrow an overbroad certification claim, but it cannot cure an unmet mandatory compliance condition when the caveat itself is the unresolved predicate.
remaining_concerns: Materiality remains triggered because the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, and no admissible evidence rebuts its status as a named launch use case or contractual customer segment.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before certification or launch in the required artifact.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for this specific unresolved named-segment gap.
Legal review remains open on whether disclosure is required, leaving a policy predicate unresolved.
